samples.summary: Workspace roll-up still returns per-document metrics for rows the caller cannot manage — the UI now hides the link, but the data behind the manager gate is already in the member-gated payload
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/analytics/analytics.controller.ts:240-252 returns every `byDocument` row (title, views, uniqueVisitors) to any workspace member, and only annotates `canManage: false` for rows whose detail dashboard is refused by packages/backend/src/analytics/analytics.controller.ts:170 (`isDocumentManager`). A plain member can read the response directly (`GET /workspaces/:wid/analytics`) and obtain per-document view/unique-visitor counts for documents authored by others — exactly the data the detail endpoint's manager gate protects at a finer grain. The new field acknowledges the two endpoints have different tiers but leaves the row payload itself ungated, so hiding the `<Link>` in packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/workspace-analytics.tsx:92 is a client-side-only restriction. Fix belongs on the new backend code (either filter/redact non-manageable rows or document that aggregate counts are intentionally member-visible). Whether member-visible aggregates are the right design is the security/design lens's call; I flag it because the guard the diff advertises has an unchanged path to adjacent data.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists (analytics.controller.ts:238-252 returns byDocument rows to any member with a canManage annotation; :170 gates the detail endpoint), but it is not a blast-radius defect. (1) No guard is bypassed: the manager gate protects warehouse.getDocumentAnalytics, whose only server call site is analytics.controller.ts:177, downstream of the gate at :170 — a repo-wide grep found no other caller. The roll-up calls a different method, getWorkspaceAnalytics (analytics-warehouse.service.ts:165-194), whose byDocument query (analytics-warehouse.service.ts:157) returns only COUNT(*)/COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id) per document and none of the gated detail payload (returningVisitors, avgDwellSeconds, byShareLink with link roles/creators/dates, byTarget). (2) canManage is an advisory UI flag, not a backend permission check: it added no precondition callers can miss and removed no data that was previously gated. The roll-up's member tier is the pre-existing, explicitly documented contract (analytics.controller.ts:220; analytics.types.ts:65-72; packages/backend/README.md:236,244; docs/design/share-link-analytics.md:212-229), which states the roll-up is member-gated while the detail dashboard is manager-gated and that canManage exists solely to avoid linking a member into a guaranteed 403. (3) What remains is whether coarse per-document counts should be member-visible — a data-tier/security design question the finding itself defers to the security lens, and which this lens explicitly excludes ("whether the new guard is the right security design"). There is no broken caller, no violated invariant, and no reachable path to the manager-gated payload, so nothing in-lane blocks.
